sections.text: Introduction

This document outlines the equipment inspection I1, 
which must be performed on an annually bases as indicated by Y1 in the title 
block.

The first draft initiated by eng. Abd El-Satar, 
EEHC technical inspection & quality control head sector, and from TL 
instructions document, 
this document certified by by eng. MPIS 
zone coordinators

Safety 
Precautions

items:
A work permit must be issued and the maintenance staff 
 should carry the suitable safety category.

Maintenance staff should be well trained, qualified or 
 directly supervised by some one who is.

Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area 
 is required.

Wear the personal protective equipment must used as safety 
 shoes, safety helmet, earplug, and gloves pairs...etc

sections.text:
Tools and 
Equipment

Safety and healthy equipment as 
 safety harnesses, cotton suit,... etc
Work to be Carried out

Make certain that the dies for aluminium and steel correspond to the prescribed 
sizes

Check whether the bores of the aluminium and of the steel joint are thoroughly 
clean
Be sure that the conductor end is not damaged if so, cut off the damaged portion
Slip the aluminium joint over the conductor for about one meter

Serve the conductor (with metallic wire, or suitable tape) at about 3 cm. off 
the end, and with a hacksaw cut off the aluminium mantle wires near the serving 
(fig. 8.a) taking care not to nick steel core wires
Serve the core end (fig. 9-b)

Serve the conductor mantle at a distance from the core end equal to half the 
steel joint length plus 25%

Cut off the aluminium wires just in front of the last serving (fig. 9-c) always 
taking care not to nick the core wires. To avoid this saw the outer 
layers of the mantle and cut only for about 2/3 of diameter the aluminium wires 
of the inner layer which are then detached by a repeated bending movement

Put a reference mark on the core (now spilled of aluminium wires) at a distance 
equal to half the steel joint length. Put the core into the steel joint as much 
as 2 cm, making the serving slipl then remove serving and push the core in up to 
the reference mark made before. To practically carry out this operation hold the 
joine by pressing it into the die fitted on compressor

Repeat operations mentioned at poines 5,6,7,8,9) on the end of the other 
corductor to be jointed and be sure that the steel joint is in the position as 
indicated on fig. 9-d

Compress the steel joint starting from the centre (fig. 9-d) working first 
toward one and then toward the other end overlapping one half of each compression 
and making sure every time that the two half dies barrel together

Clean thoroughly all alhaminium wires of conductor parts to be 
compressed. This is particulary important and shall be made by winding the 
various wire layers, especially if conductor is greassed or old and blackened in the 
first case a suitable can be used, in the second case use an emery cloth 
or a metallic brush with 2 to 3/10 mm long wires

Starting from the centre of the steel joint already compressed put a reference 
mark on each conductor at a distance eequal to half the aluminium joint length 
slip the latter over the steel joint removing obviously the serving and stop at 
the reference marks thus being sure that the aluminium joint centre corresponds 
to that the steel joint (fig. 9-a)

Compress the joint starting from the marks on the aluminium sleeve (fig 9-e) and 
work as per point 11
Assembly of joints with filter marked on the tables with cross (+) is carried 
out as above mentioned with the change of the following points
Put one conductor into one filter and into the joint making it slip for about 
one metre put the other conductor into the second filter

Put the two filters into the joint then compress the latter starting from 
the marks on the aluminium sleeve (fig. 6-a) and continuing the compression as 
mentioned at point 11

Dead ends joints and repair sleeves for monometallic conductors aluminium or 
aluminium alloy

Compression filttings for aluminium or aluminium alloy conductors are generally 
similar to those used for aluminium / steel conductors

However the steel terminals have not the tubular compression part as the 
conductors have no steel core Aluminium body can be supplied (up on request) 
already compressed onto the steel terminal in this case the position of the 
steel terminal must be stated

Joints have not, obviously the steel inner part and repair sleeves are identical 
to those supplied for aluminium steel conductors
